steps.title: Welcome!
steps.purpose: Greet the child and set emotional tone
steps.owlText: Hello friend! Today we are going to look for quarters in everyday things around us! Food, objects, nature — quarters are everywhere! Ready to go on a quarters hunt?
steps.studentText: Today we look for quarters (1/4) in everyday objects around us!

media.altText: Owl teacher waving hello with everyday objects: cake, pizza, chocolate — all cut into 4 equal parts
media.fallbackText: Owl teacher waving hello with everyday objects: cake, pizza, chocolate — all cut into 4 equal parts

steps.title: Our Mission
steps.purpose: Tell the child what they will learn
steps.studentText: Today you will learn to find quarters in everyday objects. A quarter means one of four equal parts. You will see quarters in food, paper, and things around you!

steps.title: Think First!
steps.purpose: Activate prior knowledge about quarters in real life
steps.owlText: Before we start, think about this: Can you think of something at home that you can cut or fold into four equal parts? What would each part be called?
steps.studentText: What things at home can you cut or fold into four equal parts? What is each part called?

media.altText: A home scene with various objects: cake, pizza, paper, chocolate — with question marks
media.fallbackText: A home scene with various objects: cake, pizza, paper, chocolate — with question marks

interaction.question: Name something at home that you can divide into four equal parts. What would each part be called?
interaction.placeholder: I can cut/fold... into four equal parts. Each part is...

steps.title: Learn It
steps.purpose: Teach identifying quarters in everyday objects
steps.owlText: Let me show you. When you cut a cake into four equal slices, each slice is one quarter of the cake. When you fold a paper twice to make four equal parts, each part is one quarter. When you break a chocolate bar into four equal pieces, each piece is one quarter. The key is: the four parts must be equal — the same size!
steps.studentText: A quarter in real life: Cut or fold something into four equal parts. Each part is one quarter. All four parts must be the same size!

media.altText: Three examples: (1) cake cut into 4 equal slices, (2) paper folded into 4 equal parts, (3) chocolate bar split into 4 equal pieces. Each labeled '1/4'.
media.caption: Quarters in everyday objects: cake, paper, chocolate.
media.fallbackText: Three examples: (1) cake cut into 4 equal slices, (2) paper folded into 4 equal parts, (3) chocolate bar split into 4 equal pieces. Each labeled '1/4'.

steps.title: Real Life Connection
steps.purpose: Connect quarters to many real-life contexts
steps.owlText: We see quarters everywhere! A cake cut into four equal slices. A pizza cut into four equal pieces. A paper folded into four equal parts. A chocolate bar split into four equal pieces. Even a window with four equal panes — each pane is one quarter of the window! Quarters are all around us!
steps.studentText: Quarters are everywhere: cake, pizza, paper, chocolate, windows. Look for things divided into four equal parts!

media.altText: Collage of everyday objects showing quarters: cake, pizza, paper, chocolate, window
media.fallbackText: Collage of everyday objects showing quarters: cake, pizza, paper, chocolate, window

steps.title: Watch and Learn
steps.purpose: Show worked examples of identifying quarters in objects
steps.owlText: Let me show you how to spot quarters. This cake is cut into four equal slices. Each slice is one quarter. How do I know? All four slices are the same size! This paper is folded into four equal parts. Each part is one quarter. All four parts match exactly — that is how you know they are equal.
steps.studentText: To spot quarters: Look for four parts that are the same size. If all four parts match exactly, each one is one quarter.

media.altText: Two examples: (1) cake cut into 4 equal slices with '1/4' label on each, (2) paper folded into 4 equal parts with matching edges shown.
media.fallbackText: Two examples: (1) cake cut into 4 equal slices with '1/4' label on each, (2) paper folded into 4 equal parts with matching edges shown.

steps.title: Your Turn!
steps.purpose: Practice identifying which object shows quarters
steps.owlText: Now it is your turn! Look at these two objects. One object is divided into four equal parts. The other is not. Which object shows quarters? Tap the correct one.
steps.studentText: Which object shows quarters? Look for four equal parts.

media.altText: Two objects: (A) a cake cut into 4 equal slices, (B) a cake cut into 4 unequal slices.
media.fallbackText: Two objects: (A) a cake cut into 4 equal slices, (B) a cake cut into 4 unequal slices.

interaction.question: Which object shows quarters?
options: Object A: cake cut into 4 equal slices
Object B: cake cut into 4 unequal slices
interaction.correctAnswer: Object A: cake cut into 4 equal slices
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! Object A has four equal slices. Each slice is one quarter. All parts are the same size!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Look for the object where all four parts are the same size. That is what makes quarters — four equal parts!

steps.title: Quick Check!
steps.purpose: Test understanding of quarters in real objects (QC-Q2)
steps.owlText: Quick check! A cake is cut into 4 equal slices. You eat 1 slice. What fraction of the cake did you eat?
steps.studentText: A cake is cut into 4 equal slices. You eat 1 slice. What fraction of the cake did you eat?

media.altText: A cake cut into 4 equal slices. One slice is highlighted as eaten.
media.fallbackText: A cake cut into 4 equal slices. One slice is highlighted as eaten.

interaction.question: A cake is cut into 4 equal slices. You eat 1 slice. What fraction did you eat?
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Correct! One slice out of 4 equal slices is one quarter. Well done!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: The cake was cut into 4 equal slices. You ate 1 slice. That is one quarter of the cake.

steps.title: Think About Your Learning
steps.owlText: You did great today! Think about what you learned. Where can you find quarters in everyday life? What does 'four equal parts' mean? You are a quarters detective!
steps.studentText: What did you learn about finding quarters in everyday objects?

interaction.question: How do you feel about finding quarters in everyday objects?

steps.title: You Did It!
steps.owlText: Wonderful! You learned to find quarters in everyday objects today. Look around you — quarters are in your food, your paper, your world! Keep being a quarters detective!
steps.studentText: You learned to find quarters in everyday objects! Look for quarters everywhere!

media.altText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says 'I found quarters!'
media.fallbackText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says 'I found quarters!'
